user.title: Electricity prices
user.description: Pick the integration that supplies your prices, and the sensor that carries the upcoming ones. The planner needs future prices, not just the current one — usually that is the 'average price' sensor, which keeps the whole day in an attribute.

price_keys.title: Where the prices live
price_keys.description: Name the attribute holding the list of upcoming prices, and the keys inside each entry. You can look these up under Developer tools → States by selecting the sensor and reading its attributes.

charger.title: Charger
charger.description: The switch is the one thing that is required: it is what gets turned on and off at the planned moments. The two sensors are optional and only improve the measured charging speed.

car.title: Car
car.description: Linking a car is optional. Without one you simply tell the planner how many kWh you want; with one it works that out from the charge level.

car_details.title: Car details
car_details.description: The charge level is read passively. If a refresh button is set, it is pressed at most once when you open the planner page and only when the reading is older than the age below — never on a timer, because some cars wake their modem to answer and drain their 12V battery.

defaults.title: Defaults
defaults.description: Starting values. All of these stay adjustable afterwards, and the charging speed can be replaced later by the speed actually measured.

abort.already_configured: That charging switch is already planned by another entry.

init.title: Electricity prices
init.description: Change the price source. Leaving it as it is and clicking through gets you to the other steps.

apply_suggestion.name: Start charging
apply_suggestion.description: Work out the cheapest moments before the deadline and commit them as the schedule.

stop.name: Stop
stop.description: Clear the schedule and switch the charger off.

refresh_car.name: Refresh car
refresh_car.description: Ask the car for a fresh charge level, but only if the reading is stale and the rate limit allows it. Intended to be called when a dashboard opens, never on a schedule.

adopt_measured_power.name: Adopt measured charging speed
adopt_measured_power.description: Replace the configured charging power with the speed measured over recent sessions.
